
Two arXiv papers from the RSS feed meet ≥3 inclusion criteria with strong relevance to agentic workflow design: Lean4Agent addresses formal modeling and verification of agent workflows and trajectories (architectural guidance, execution lifecycle, evaluation loops, empirical grounding), and the Declarative Skills paper addresses tool-use workflow design with knowledge grounding (tool-use design, architectural patterns, practical grounding). Grok social signals were generic/unverifiable URLs and not proposed.

## Suggestions

- [Lean4Agent: Formal Modeling and Verification for Agent Workflow and Trajectory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06523) — Applies formal modeling and verification (via Lean4) to agent workflows and execution trajectories, providing rigorous architectural grounding for correctness, state management, and evaluation of agentic systems.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (patterns, orchestration, state management), Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Iterative refinement practices (evaluation loops, human-in-the-loop, observability), Empirical or practical grounding (case studies, benchmarks, production deployment evidence)

- [Declarative Skills for AI Agents in Knowledge-Grounded Tool-Use Workflows](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06923) — Proposes a declarative skill abstraction for structuring knowledge-grounded tool-use workflows in AI agents, addressing tool selection, workflow composition, and execution design across the agent lifecycle.
  Section: Research Papers | Criteria: Architectural guidance for goal-directed agent systems (patterns, orchestration, state management), Tool-use and execution design across agent lifecycle stages (planning, execution, feedback, recovery), Empirical or practical grounding (case studies, benchmarks, production deployment evidence)
